title: Finance and cash
purpose: When cash runs tight, a payout is late, a sale looked better than it was or a tax letter lands, open Finance and cash to see what is really left, when it runs out and what to do first.
fires: the bookkeeper's month-old profit report, the Sunday cash spreadsheet, the call to the accountant to ask if we are ok, and the habit of reading the bank balance as the plan.
not_for: a brand that wants its books kept or its taxes filed; this is for deciding with money, not for doing the accounting.

jobs.job: When the bank balance looks thin 2 weeks before a supplier deposit and payroll, tell me the lowest cash day in the next 13 weeks and what to move, so I make payroll without a panic loan
jobs.circumstance: mid-month, the bank shows less than it felt like it should, a $60,000 supplier deposit and payroll land the same week, a partner asks if we are ok

progress.functional: know the lowest cash day, how far below the floor it goes, and the 3 moves that fix it
progress.emotional: stop the 3 am bank app checks and the fear of missing payroll
progress.social: answer a partner, lender or team with a date and a plan, not a shrug

jobs.hire_today: a cash spreadsheet rebuilt on Sundays, a fractional finance lead, or the bank balance and gut feel
jobs.fire: the Sunday spreadsheet and the habit of reading the bank balance as the plan

forces.push: a profitable brand can still miss payroll
forces.pull: a 13 week cash line with the low point, its date and the moves that lift it
forces.habit: the bank balance has always been the check
forces.anxiety: what if the forecast is wrong and I delay a bill for nothing

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and the day any big bill or deposit is agreed

watch.metric: lowest projected cash balance in the next 13 weeks against the cash floor, weekly
watch.source: bank feed, payouts, open bills and purchase orders in the brand brain

drives.metric: weeks of cash runway at the current burn

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: cash dips $22,000 below the floor in week 6, nobody sees it. After: seen 5 weeks ahead, a deposit moved and a slow product cleared, low point stays $15,000 above the floor.
jobs.not_for: a brand with a year of cash in the bank and no stock bets, where a monthly look is enough

jobs.job: When a payout I counted on has not landed on the day I expected, tell me which one, why and when it will arrive, so I can chase it or move a payment
jobs.circumstance: a Tuesday, a supplier payment goes out tomorrow, the Shopify, PayPal or marketplace payout expected yesterday is not in the bank

progress.functional: know each expected payout, its date and which ones are late or short
progress.emotional: stop the sick feeling of money gone missing
progress.social: tell the supplier a true date instead of an excuse

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper who checks weekly, the founder refreshing the bank app, or nothing
jobs.fire: the daily bank refresh and the habit of finding late payouts at month end

forces.push: a late payout breaks the week's plan
forces.pull: every payout expected against landed, with the reason for any gap
forces.anxiety: what if chasing the processor flags the account

jobs.little_hire: every payout day, and whenever the bank looks light

watch.metric: payouts late or short against expected, by source, daily
watch.source: Shopify Payments, PayPal, installment lenders and marketplace settlement reports joined to the bank feed

drives.metric: days from order to cash in the bank, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $14,000 payout 6 days late, found when a supplier payment bounced. After: late payouts flagged the next morning, 0 bounced payments.
jobs.not_for: a brand with one payment processor that always pays on the same day

jobs.job: When my team wants to run a 25 percent off sitewide sale next week, tell me the sales lift it needs to break even after product cost, shipping, fees and returns, so we do not run a sale that loses money
jobs.circumstance: the promo is on the calendar, creative is being made, nobody has done the math at the discounted price

progress.functional: know the break-even lift and the profit at a likely lift
progress.emotional: stop the worry that a busy week is a losing week
progress.social: give the team a yes, a no or a smaller offer with the numbers

jobs.hire_today: a quick spreadsheet, the agency's past sale, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the last-minute gut call and the habit of discounting because it worked last time

forces.push: a deep sale can need a lift the brand never gets
forces.pull: break-even lift and profit per order at the sale price
forces.anxiety: what if we skip it and the competitor's sale takes our customers

jobs.little_hire: before every sale, code, bundle or gift with purchase

watch.metric: profit per order at the sale price against break-even, per promo
watch.source: orders, landed cost, shipping, fees and return rate in the brand brain

drives.metric: contribution margin per promo week against a normal week

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 25 percent sale needs a 70 percent lift to break even and gets 40 percent. After: the sale is cut to 15 percent on 20 products and makes $12,000 more.
jobs.not_for: a brand that never discounts

jobs.job: When my agency asks for 30 percent more ad budget next month, tell me the most I can spend and still make money, from total sales and total spend, so I say yes or no with a number
jobs.circumstance: month-end, the agency sends a plan with a bigger number, platform returns look strong, the bank does not feel it

progress.functional: know the spend ceiling where profit after ads stays above target
progress.emotional: stop feeling bullied by numbers I cannot check
progress.social: answer the agency with a firm, reasoned limit

jobs.hire_today: the agency's own plan, platform return numbers, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the agency's platform numbers and the habit of saying yes when returns look good

forces.push: platforms claim the same sale twice, so budgets grow on air
forces.pull: a ceiling from total store sales per ad dollar and profit per order
forces.anxiety: what if I cap spend just before it would have scaled

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and at every budget request

watch.metric: total store sales divided by total ad spend against the break-even line, weekly
watch.source: store orders and ad spend from every platform

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: spend up 30 percent last quarter, profit after ads flat. After: a ceiling of $90,000 a month set, profit after ads up $14,000.
jobs.not_for: a brand spending under a few thousand a month on ads

jobs.job: When the accountant says we made a profit but there is no cash, show me where the profit went, stock, payouts, loan payments, so I stop feeling lied to by my own numbers
jobs.circumstance: the quarterly call with the accountant, the profit report says $80,000 profit, the bank says otherwise, the founder does not know which to believe

progress.functional: see profit turned into cash, line by line: stock bought, payouts pending, loans repaid, tax paid
progress.emotional: stop feeling foolish about my own business
progress.social: explain it to a partner in 2 minutes

jobs.hire_today: the accountant's explanation once a quarter, or nothing
jobs.fire: the quarterly confusion and the habit of trusting only the bank balance

forces.push: decisions are made on a profit that is not in the bank
forces.pull: a simple bridge from profit to cash each month
forces.habit: the accountant explains it and it fades
forces.anxiety: what if the bridge shows I made a big mistake

watch.metric: gap between monthly profit and change in cash, with the named causes, monthly
watch.source: books, bank feed, inventory value and loan schedule

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $80,000 profit, cash down $30,000, no one knows why. After: $95,000 traced to stock bought early and $15,000 to a payout held, next buy resized.
jobs.not_for: a brand whose profit and cash already move together because it holds little stock

jobs.job: When a letter from a state tax office says we owe sales tax, tell me what we owe, since when, and which other states are next, so I settle it once and stop the penalties
jobs.circumstance: a letter arrives, a state claims unpaid sales tax for 2 years, the accountant is on holiday, the amount is a guess

progress.functional: know the real amount owed per state and the other states over the limit
progress.emotional: stop the fear of more letters
progress.social: work with the accountant from facts, not panic

jobs.hire_today: an accountant, a sales tax lawyer, a sales tax app, or nothing until the letter came
jobs.fire: the panicked calls and the habit of assuming a small store does not owe

forces.push: penalties and interest grow every month
forces.pull: sales per state against each state's limit, back to the date we crossed it
forces.anxiety: what if looking finds more we owe

jobs.little_hire: when a notice arrives, then each quarter

watch.metric: states where sales passed the limit without registration, quarterly
watch.source: orders by ship-to state and the brand brain tax register

drives.metric: sales tax owed but not collected, running total

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 notice for $18,000 and 3 other states over the limit unknown. After: all 4 registered, voluntary filings cut penalties, 0 new notices.
jobs.not_for: a brand selling only in its home state, or already using a tax service that files every state

jobs.job: When revenue is up but the bank is not, show me what each product and channel really made after every cost, so I grow the right ones
jobs.circumstance: the monthly review, sales up 20 percent on last year, profit flat, the team wants to push the best sellers harder

progress.functional: see profit per order, product and channel after product cost, shipping, fees, returns and ads
progress.emotional: stop growing things that quietly lose money
progress.social: decide the plan with a partner on the same numbers

jobs.hire_today: a fractional finance lead's quarterly model, a bookkeeper's profit report, or nothing
jobs.fire: the quarterly model and the habit of reading revenue as success

forces.push: growth is spent on the wrong products and channels
forces.pull: a ranked list of what makes and loses money, every month
forces.anxiety: what if the cost data is wrong and I cut a winner

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before every budget or stock decision

watch.metric: contribution margin per product and channel after marketing, monthly
watch.source: orders, landed cost, shipping, fees, returns and ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of the top 10 products lose money after shipping and returns. After: 2 repriced, 1 cut, margin up $9,000 a month.
jobs.not_for: a brand with one product and one channel, where the profit report is already the answer

jobs.job: When a supplier wants a 50 percent deposit on our biggest order ever, show me what it does to cash for the next 6 months, so I do not empty the bank for stock that sells in spring
jobs.circumstance: a purchase order is ready to sign, the supplier wants the deposit this week, the stock sells over 5 months

progress.functional: see cash each week with and without the order, and a smaller order that works
progress.emotional: stop gambling the business on one purchase order
progress.social: negotiate terms with the supplier with a real limit

jobs.hire_today: the founder's gut, a spreadsheet, or the supplier's minimum order
jobs.fire: the gut call and the habit of ordering big to get the unit price

forces.push: one purchase order can drain cash for months
forces.pull: cash line with the purchase order shown, and the order size cash can carry
forces.habit: bigger orders are cheaper per unit
forces.anxiety: what if a smaller order runs out in peak

watch.metric: lowest cash point in 26 weeks with the purchase order against the cash floor, per purchase order
watch.source: purchase orders, cash forecast and sales plan

drives.metric: cash tied up in stock, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $120,000 purchase order would take cash $25,000 below the floor in month 3. After: split into 2 drops, low point $20,000 above the floor, unit cost up 2 percent.

jobs.job: When a wholesale buyer is 45 days late on an invoice, show me who owes what and since when, so I chase it before it becomes bad debt

progress.emotional: stop the awkward feeling of chasing friends
progress.social: keep the relationship while getting paid

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper, the invoicing tool, or nothing

forces.push: money owed is cash we cannot spend
forces.pull: a list of what each buyer owes and since when, with a reminder ready
forces.anxiety: what if chasing loses the account

watch.metric: money owed by wholesale buyers over 30 days late, weekly
watch.source: invoicing tool and books

drives.metric: days from wholesale invoice to cash, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $42,000 owed, $18,000 over 45 days. After: under $5,000 over 45 days within 60 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no wholesale or invoiced sales

jobs.job: When the processor starts holding 20 percent of payouts as a reserve, tell me why, how long and what it does to cash, so I can plan and get it released
jobs.circumstance: a payout lands short, a reserve notice sits in the inbox, a supplier bill is due Friday

watch.metric: amount held in processor reserves, weekly
watch.source: Shopify Payments, Stripe or PayPal payout reports

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $35,000 held with no date. After: cause found (chargeback rate), fixed, reserve released in 60 days.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no processor holds

jobs.job: When the Black Friday sale looked great on revenue, show me what it made after product cost, shipping, fees and returns, so I know before I run it again
jobs.circumstance: early December, the revenue number was the biggest of the year, returns are still coming in, the team wants to repeat it

forces.push: the next sale gets planned on the wrong lesson
forces.pull: profit per sale with returns counted as they land

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $400,000 in sale revenue, profit unknown. After: the sale made $31,000 after returns; next year the discount drops 10 points on low-margin products.

jobs.job: When Black Friday is 8 weeks out, plan spend, stock and cash together, so I do not run out of cash in November or stock in December

progress.functional: see spend, stock and cash on one weekly plan
progress.emotional: stop dreading peak
progress.social: align the agency, warehouse and supplier on one plan

jobs.hire_today: separate plans from the agency and the operations lead, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the 3 separate plans and the habit of hoping they fit

forces.push: peak is the biggest cash swing of the year
forces.pull: one weekly plan for spend, stock and cash through January
forces.habit: each team plans its own part
forces.anxiety: what if demand is much higher or lower

jobs.little_hire: weekly from 8 weeks before peak to 4 weeks after

watch.metric: lowest cash in the peak plan against the floor, weekly
watch.source: ad plan, purchase orders and cash forecast

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: last year cash went $30,000 below the floor in November. After: plan keeps cash $10,000 above, 0 stockouts on top products.
jobs.not_for: a brand without a strong peak season

jobs.job: When I tell an investor our revenue, count wholesale, Amazon, TikTok Shop and retail too, net of their fees, so I do not undersell the business
jobs.circumstance: an investor call next week, the Shopify number is the only one handy, a third of sales happen elsewhere

progress.emotional: stop feeling the story is smaller than the business
progress.social: look in command of the numbers to an investor

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper's month-end pull, a spreadsheet stitched from 5 exports, or nothing
jobs.fire: the stitched spreadsheet and the habit of quoting the Shopify number

forces.push: channels outside the store are underrated and underfunded
forces.pull: every channel's sales and fees in one total
forces.habit: Shopify is the number we know
forces.anxiety: what if channels are counted twice

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any investor or lender meeting

watch.metric: share of total revenue from outside the online store, monthly
watch.source: store, marketplace settlements, wholesale invoices and retail reports

drives.metric: total revenue across all channels, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: investor told $2.1 million from Shopify. After: $3.2 million across 5 channels, with profit per channel.

jobs.job: When 6 bills are due the same week and cash is short, tell me which to pay now and which can wait without harm, so we keep suppliers happy and cash above the floor
jobs.circumstance: a tight week, bills from the warehouse, 2 suppliers, the agency, rent and software, cash covers 4

progress.functional: rank bills by due date, penalty and relationship risk
progress.emotional: stop the dread of choosing who not to pay
progress.social: keep the key suppliers' trust

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper's advice, the founder's gut, or paying whoever shouts loudest
jobs.fire: the loudest-first habit

forces.push: the wrong bill paid late costs stock or a late fee
forces.pull: a ranked pay list that keeps cash above the floor
forces.anxiety: what if a supplier stops shipping

watch.metric: bills paid late and late fees paid, monthly
watch.source: books and bank feed

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $1,800 in late fees last quarter, 1 supplier on hold. After: 0 late fees, 0 holds, 2 bills moved with agreement.

jobs.job: When a new tariff is announced on goods we import, show me what it does to each product's margin and cash, so I reprice or reorder before it lands
jobs.circumstance: news of a tariff change, effective in weeks, stock is on the water, the next purchase order is due

progress.functional: know margin per product after the new duty and the cash needed at landing
progress.emotional: stop the panic of a cost shock

jobs.hire_today: a customs broker, an accountant, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the rough guess and the habit of absorbing cost rises

forces.push: margin drops on every unit once it lands

jobs.little_hire: each tariff or freight change, and each purchase order

watch.metric: landed cost and margin per product at the new duty rate, per purchase order
watch.source: landed cost in the brand brain and supplier invoices

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 15 point duty rise would cut margin to 38 percent on 12 products. After: 8 repriced, 1 resourced, margin held at 52 percent.
jobs.not_for: a brand that makes and sells in the same country with no imported parts

jobs.job: When Shopify Capital or a revenue loan offers $150,000 in one click, show me the real cost and what repayments do to cash, so I do not take money that traps me
jobs.circumstance: an offer email, cash is tight, the money would fund Q4 stock, the fee looks small

progress.functional: know the true yearly cost and the cash left after repayments each week
progress.emotional: stop the fear of both saying no and saying yes
progress.social: explain the choice to a partner

jobs.hire_today: an accountant, a friend who raised money, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the one-click accept and the habit of comparing only the fee

watch.metric: true yearly cost of each financing offer and lowest cash with repayments
watch.source: offer terms and the cash forecast

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $150,000 advance with a fee that works out to 28 percent a year. After: $80,000 taken instead, low point stays above the floor.

jobs.job: When Shopify says one number, the processor another and the bookkeeper a third, tell me which is right and why they differ, so I stop the monthly argument

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper's monthly reconcile, or nothing

forces.push: every decision and every tax filing rests on a guess

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $9,000 gap each month, no named cause. After: gap under $300, each part named.

jobs.job: When the accountant says we owe $40,000 in income tax next month, show it coming months ahead, so it is set aside, not found

jobs.hire_today: the accountant once a year, or nothing
jobs.fire: the yearly surprise

jobs.job: When I want to take money out for myself, tell me what I can safely draw this month without hurting the cash plan, so I stop paying myself last out of fear

jobs.fire: the habit of paying myself last or never

jobs.job: When a supplier raises cost by 12 percent, tell me the new price I need to keep my margin and what it might do to sales, so I reprice once, not by feel
